message:
Fuse chained bignum +/- into in-place accumulation

a + b + c + d (compiled bottom-up as nested Binary nodes) allocated a
fresh bignum_new for every intermediate result, even though each one
is immediately superseded by the next op and never read again.

Profiled first with a standalone GMP microbenchmark, using the exact
shim functions codegen already calls (bignum_new/add/free copied
verbatim from runtime/gmp/bignum_shim.c), before writing any compiler
code: ~1.8-2.0x for one extra chained term, ~2.7-3.2x for a 4-op chain
-- confirmed matching in the real compiler afterward (~2.5x on a
2,000,000-iteration 5-term-chain loop, unfused baseline measured
directly via a stash rather than trusted from the microbenchmark).

No new chain-detection AST walk needed: a left-associative chain
already compiles bottom-up through the existing recursive compile_expr
structure, so the only change is in the bignum-vs-bignum dispatch's
destination selection. For Add/Sub specifically, when the left
operand's compiled value is itself a live (not-yet-consumed)
bignum_temps entry at exactly this op's own result precision -- the
identical matching technique compile_and_coerce's adoption check
(99411f8) already uses, just applied one step earlier, at allocation
time rather than storage time -- reuse that handle as the destination
(GMP documents mpf_add/mpf_sub's destination may alias a source
operand) instead of allocating a new one. The precision guard is what
makes this safe when a chain widens partway through: a too-narrow
buffer is never reused, since a mpf_t's precision is fixed at
construction and mpf_add respects the destination's own precision, not
the operands'.

Deliberately only Add/Sub -- Mul/Div/Pow chains weren't profiled and
GMP's aliasing guarantee wasn't independently verified for them here,
left as a possible future extension rather than assumed to transfer.

Verified: mixed +/- chains, a repeated operand, a chain that widens
partway through (correctly falls back to a fresh allocation for that
step), a chain result feeding a further op, an 8-term chain, the same
chain evaluated twice (no double-adopt/free), high-precision
propagation through a fully-fused chain (a repeating-decimal check,
not just small integers indistinguishable across precisions), and no
leak/double-free across 2,000,000 repeated calls to a function
containing a chain (identical peak memory footprint vs. 50 calls).
Full example-suite regression pass.
